doc.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: The banjo, rhythm and the New Orleans style
title: His rhythm on Sidney Bechet's Summertime recording
summary: White points out Barker's rhythm on Bechet's Summertime, and Barker recalls how Bechet gave no praise but seemed pleased.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: I noticed you did just that thing on my favorite recording of Summertime by Sidney Bechet. It’s one that you played. You were on the record. Do you remember that recording?
You recorded Summertime and some other things. It’s on a record called The Genius of Sidney Bechet.
It sounds great, and I think what set the background and the foundation for what Bechet was playing was the way you played those rhythms, and I could hear you doing that in there.

That’s why it was the thing. Bechet understood that. He understand that brought back memories to him. I know that because I see . . . what I done, when I start playing, I look to see his expression [ ? (inaudible)], but he felt pleased. He didn’t give me credit, said “This is great” or nothing, because he was like that. He don’t give you credit for
But you could tell that he is very relaxed and comfortable.
